html:
The Guugu Yimithirr are an Aboriginal Australian people of the country around Cooktown in north Queensland, on the eastern side of Cape York. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

In 1770 James Cook's ship Endeavour struck the Great Barrier Reef and spent about seven weeks beached for repairs in the river mouth here. It was the longest stay of the voyage on Australian soil. The crew wrote down words of the local language, including gangurru, which became the English word "kangaroo". A quarrel broke out when the sailors would not share turtles they had caught, and it ended with a meeting at which the two sides made peace.

Their language is also known among linguists because speakers give directions by the compass, north, south, east and west, rather than left and right. The Palmer River gold rush of 1873 made Cooktown a busy port and took their land. Neighbours on the map include the Kokowarra and the Kuku Yalanji. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
sum: The Guugu Yimithirr are an Aboriginal Australian people of the country around Cooktown in north Queensland, on the eastern side of Cape York. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.
